extracted.intended_audience: USDA awarding agencies, grant applicants and recipients, research institutions, USDA program staff, and other stakeholders in Federal financial assistance
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed revisions to USDA's adoption and supplementation of the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards (2 CFR Chapter IV), including policy changes, plain-language edits, technical corrections, and new parts addressing procurement, competition, debarment, lobbying, research misconduct, and geospatial data disclosures. The document explains proposed regulatory text, reasons for changes, and how the revisions affect agencies, recipients, and procedural obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized definitions for 2 CFR Chapter IV
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a new definition section applicable to 2 CFR Chapter IV which centralizes existing definitions from current parts of 2 CFR Chapter IV and defines for USDA certain terms present in 2 CFR Subtitle A but not defined in that subtitle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralization provides clarity, reduces agency and recipient burden on interpretation and application, enhances uniform interpretation and application of 2 CFR Subtitle A and 2 CFR Chapter IV, and will improve management, transparency, and oversight of USDA Federal financial assistance awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest requirements for awarding agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies conflict of interest requirements applicable to each USDA awarding agency, including implementation of procedures to identify, disclose, and mitigate identified conflicts of interest that may arise during the period of performance of an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying conflict of interest requirements reduces agency burden and improves management and oversight of USDA awards; the proposed language identifies timeframes for discovery of conflicts to enable uniform approaches across USDA awarding agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build America, Buy America (BABA) waiver policy (Part 401)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds a new part 401 identifying USDA policy for implementation of waivers to the Build America, Buy America (BABA) Act domestic content procurement preferences for Federal financial assistance programs and projects, as required by 2 CFR 184.7b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed language ensures USDA compliance with statutory requirements and transparently identifies processes by which USDA ensures full compliance with requirements related to issuing waivers to BABA domestic content procurement preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of notices of funding opportunities (competition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies requirements related to the competition of discretionary grants and cooperative agreements, including dissemination of notices of funding opportunities to foster innovation, competition, and diversity in applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad dissemination and focus on identifying the greatest number and diversity of potential applicants may decrease burden on prospective first-time applicants and increase innovation and competition for discretionary awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review procedures and selection of independent reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies selection of independent reviewers for the conduct of merit review and clarifies conflict of interests related to the conduct of merit review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed language enhances conduct of merit review at USDA by providing clarification and additional direction on USDA awarding agency procedures to ensure impartial, transparent review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of unsolicited applications and related materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernizes requirements for treatment of unsolicited applications and related materials to reflect digitization of grants administration processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernization will decrease agency burden while retaining flexibility and discretion to make awards following unsolicited applications and aligns processes with modern, digital workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompetitive justification statements and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernizes noncompetitive justification statements, updates transparency requirements, and requires any additional noncompetitive justification statements established by USDA awarding agencies be made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates enhance transparency of noncompetitive awards, identify agency flexibility in establishing exceptions to competition (subject to approval by the Secretary and OMB), and decrease burden on prospective applicants unfamiliar with noncompetitive programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently governmental functions considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporates direction related to inherently governmental functions as established by OFPP Policy Letter 11-01, including considerations related to financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change strengthens administration of financial assistance by providing clear direction to USDA awarding agencies about functions that should remain governmental and clarifies boundaries between agency responsibilities and recipient/contractor roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of USDA support on information products
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernizes the requirements for acknowledgement of USDA support on information dissemination products, expanding terminology beyond 'publications and audiovisuals' to cover digital products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expansion ensures broad coverage of materials produced with USDA Federal financial assistance support and updates language established in 1981 to reflect digital products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical corrections to procurement citations (Part 416)
rubrics_metrics.description: Makes technical correction to the citation to 2 CFR 200.101(f) in paragraphs (a) and (b) to refer to parts 4 through 7 and removes citation to 2 CFR 200.319(c) in paragraph (b) as conforming updates to OMB's April 22, 2024 updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections are technical in nature and intended to fix citation errors without changing program delivery or operations; plain language updates ensure currency and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprocurement debarment and suspension updates (Part 417)
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes language duplicative of 2 CFR part 180, makes conforming updates to USDA supplements to 2 CFR part 180, and proposes plain language updates and technical corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing duplicative language streamlines USDA regulations, decreases applicant burden in understanding debarment and suspension requirements, and updates references (e.g., former EPLS system consolidated into SAM.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: New restrictions on lobbying updates (Part 418)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescinds Subpart F and makes conforming updates including recission of Appendix B to Part 418; plain language updates and technical corrections are proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart F was removed from OMB government-wide guidance in 1996; removal clarifies expectations, reduces administrative burden, and ensures USDA and public access only to the most updated SF-LLL form (available on Grants.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug-free workplace technical corrections (Part 421)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopts OMB guidance in subparts A through F of 2 CFR part 182 as supplemented and proposes technical corrections to citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical corrections ensure currency of information available to the public; no substantive policy change is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct: institutional responsibilities (Part 422 §422.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A research institution that conducts extramural research funded by USDA bears primary responsibility for prevention and detection of research misconduct and for the inquiry, investigation, and adjudication of research misconduct allegations reported directly to it; must perform an inquiry and, if warranted, an investigation; adjudication responsibilities must be separate from inquiry and investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most instances USDA will rely on institutions to promptly: initiate inquiries, conduct investigations if warranted, acquire/prepare/maintain appropriate records, and take actions to ensure integrity, protect rights/interests of subjects and the public, observe legal requirements, and safeguard complainants and subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct: notifications, content of allegations, and safeguards (§§422.6, 422.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must promptly notify OIG and USDA RIO when institutional inquiry warrants investigation; formal allegations should include project names, nature of alleged misconduct, names involved, funding sources, dates, documentation, and other relevant information; safeguards for complainants include protection against retaliation and confidentiality when requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG hotline and contact details provided; safeguards increase confidence in reporting and include timely written notification to subjects, access to evidence, opportunity to respond, and confidentiality to extent permitted by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review of institution policies and USDA reservation of authority (§§422.4, 422.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before USDA will rely on an institution for proceedings, the institution must provide its research misconduct policies/procedures for review by a USDA panel (RIO and ARIOs); the Panel will assess compliance with OSTP policy. USDA reserves the right to conduct its own inquiry/investigation/adjudication if institution procedures are insufficient, not followed, biased, untimely, or for other appropriate reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Panel determines institution procedures are insufficient, USDA will inform the institution and an appropriate USDA agency will conduct proceedings; when USDA conducts proceedings it will require documentation of institution actions to date and act under Agency procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research records and evidence custody, handling, and retention (§§422.9, 422.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must maintain specified documents related to allegations (original allegation statement, notification to subject, inquiry and investigation reports, methods, evidentiary records, findings, corrective actions) and retain them for at least 3 years following final adjudication. When investigations are initiated, institutions must promptly obtain custody of relevant records/evidence, inventory and securely store originals, and if copying data from devices is necessary it must be done by a disinterested qualified technician.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing obligation to create and maintain adequate records; copies must be complete and accurate with equivalent evidentiary value; secure inventory and storage procedures protect the integrity of evidence for subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for research misconduct noncompliance and proportionality (§422.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency implementation procedures identify administrative actions available to remedy findings of research misconduct (e.g., recovery of funds, correction of the research record, debarment, proper attribution, or other appropriate actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency should consider seriousness, intentionality, pattern, and impact on research record/subjects/public welfare; remedies must be commensurate with the infraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process for research misconduct findings (§422.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If USDA relied on an institution to conduct proceedings, alleged persons should first follow the institution's appeal policy; USDA agencies' implementation procedures (posted on public USDA website) identify appeal processes when findings are elevated to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions and agencies must make appeal procedures available and accessible; initial reliance on institution-level appeal processes is expected before USDA-level appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to other agency requirements (§422.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some research may be subject to other federal agency regulations; when more than one agency has jurisdiction USDA will cooperate in designating a lead agency, rely on the lead agency's policies when not the lead, and may take actions in consultation to protect public health/safety, research integrity, or conserve public funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USDA will seek to resolve allegations jointly when appropriate and coordinate with other agencies to ensure consistent handling across federal funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geospatial data disclosure requirements (Part 423)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implements 43 U.S.C. 2808(b)(3) by requiring that Federal financial assistance instruments involving acquisition, storage, or distribution of geospatial data include terms and conditions requiring recipients to comply with law, regulation, and USDA policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USDA awarding agencies must ensure award terms and conditions necessary for complying with law/regulation/USDA policy are included to ensure uniform application of disclosure requirements across USDA financial assistance instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Orders and economic/regulatory review expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Orders 12866 and 13563 direct agencies to assess costs and benefits of regulatory alternatives and select approaches that maximize net benefits, including assessing distributive impacts and equity. OMB designated this proposed rule as not significant under EO 12866.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should quantify costs and benefits, reduce costs, harmonize rules, promote flexibility. The document states the proposed rule contains no Federal mandates as defined by UMRA and has no information collection requirements under the Paperwork Reduction Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: USDA Non-Discrimination Policy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: USDA, its agencies, employees, and institutions participating in or administering USDA programs are prohibited from discriminating based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, marital or family status, income from public assistance, political beliefs, or reprisal/retaliation for prior civil rights activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies and complaint filing deadlines vary by program; individuals requiring alternative communication means should contact USDA TARGET Center; program information may be available in other languages.
